guideTitle: 6 Best Power Recliners With USB Ports in 2026
metaTitle: Best Power Recliners With USB Ports (2026)
metaDescription: Six power recliners with built-in USB charging compared on port placement, seat size, cup holders and upholstery for everyday living rooms.
introParagraphs: Charging a phone or tablet from the chair you are already sitting in sounds minor until the cable is too short and the outlet is across the room. A power recliner with USB ports builds that convenience into the armrest or control panel, so the device stays within reach while you read, watch or video call. The six chairs below all include USB charging, though the ports sit in different places and the chairs around them vary widely.

We evaluated each model from product specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on testing. Port location, seat size, recline method and cover material separate them far more than the ports themselves. A chair that charges a phone beautifully but does not fit the person who sits in it is not a good purchase.

These are comfort chairs, not medical equipment, and they should not be treated as a way to prevent falls or manage health conditions. Weight capacity, correct setup and a safe cable path all matter. An occupational or physical therapist can advise on fit when mobility is a concern, since needs differ from person to person.

products.name: CANMOV Electric Power Recliner with USB Ports
products.description:
The CANMOV measures 36 inches wide, 35 inches deep and 41 inches high, with a 23 by 23 inch seat set 19 inches off the floor. Breathable leather-look upholstery covers a high-density sponge cushion, and the armrests include dual cup holders and storage. USB ports come built in, alongside a simple electric recline.

The listing openly asks buyers to confirm the dimensions before ordering, which is good advice for any recliner. A 23-inch square seat is roomy for most adults without being oversized, so it suits a standard living room. It does not add heat or massage, which keeps the controls plain.

In ownership the chair behaves like a normal power recliner: place it near an outlet, leave room behind it and wipe the cover as needed. A second CANMOV variant exists with a 24 by 20 inch seat, so double-check which size you are ordering. Compared with the ANJ, the CANMOV is more focused on seating than on gadgets.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a standard-size recliner with charging and cup holders.
pros: Roomy 23 by 23 inch seat for most adults
Seat sits 19 inches off the floor
Dual cup holders with armrest storage
USB charging ports come built in
cons: No heat or massage functions listed
A similar model has a shallower seat

products.name: jonpony Power Lift Recliner with USB, Massage and Heat
products.description:
The jonpony is the only lift chair in this lineup, because its power lift can raise the entire recliner from its base. It offers eight massage points, two intensity settings, heat and a skin-friendly fabric cover filled with enough padding for long sitting.

Only the jonpony adds the lift function, which changes how the chair is used for people who stand slowly from soft seats. The tradeoff is a more complex base and a heavier chair than the ANJ or Amada. Lift chairs should be fitted to the user, and a therapist can advise.

Port placement and the remote layout matter more on a chair like this, so confirm both on the listing before buying. A fabric cover will soak up spills more than the PU leather on the ANJ, so use a cover if the chair is a snack spot. Next to the Ketaiyou, the jonpony trades swivel and rocking for lifting.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants lift assist together with USB charging.

products.name: Ketaiyou Power Swivel Rocker Recliner, Dark Grey
products.description:
The Ketaiyou mixes a 270-degree swivel with rocking, electric recline between 90 and 160 degrees, and massage with heat. Built-in USB sits beside dual side pockets and two cup holders, one on each side, so right-handed and left-handed users are both covered.

Swivel and rock add movement that most recliners lack, which suits people who like to turn toward a conversation or window. The extra parts do mean more joints to keep clean and a larger footprint, and swivel bases need free space around them. Rocking should be locked or stopped before standing.

Setup involves attaching the base and the swivel plate, so allow time and a second pair of hands. It offers a wider recline sweep than the ANJ's listed controls and adds motion the CANMOV and Amada do not. The dark grey colour is easy to match with most room schemes.
products.bestFor: People who want swivel and rocking along with USB charging.
pros: 270-degree swivel helps you face anyone

Cup holders on both sides suit either hand
Massage and heat plus USB in one chair
cons: Swivel base needs clear space around it
More moving parts to keep clean

products.name: MAHOMICO Power Lift Recliner, USB and Cup Holders
products.description:
The MAHOMICO is billed as an oversized single sofa with electric lift and recline. Eight vibration massage points target the back, thighs and calves, lumbar heating is included, and a USB charging port keeps a phone or tablet powered alongside the cup holders.

It is the only oversized pick here with both lift and charging, which makes it a natural option for larger frames. The tradeoff is footprint and weight, and the listing does not list seat measurements. Check the maker's sheet for width, depth and weight rating before ordering.

In ownership the chair is a big presence, so confirm doorway width and plan where the cord will run. A larger seat gives more room than the CANMOV's 23-inch width, but it also needs more floor. Compared with the jonpony, the MAHOMICO offers a roomier feel at the cost of space.

pros: Oversized seating suits larger frames

products.name: ANJ Power Recliner with USB Ports and Cup Holders
products.description:
The ANJ uses two buttons to move the footrest and backrest, and its two USB ports sit on the controls on the outer side of the armrest. PU leather is described as breathable and moisture resistant, and there are two cup holders plus hidden armrest storage.

Placing the ports with the controls keeps everything on one spot, which is easy to learn. There is no heat or massage, so the remote stays minimal. The overstuffed styling looks like theatre seating and gives the chair a stronger look than the Amada.

Wipe-clean PU is a plus for a family room, though it can feel warm in summer. Hidden armrest storage keeps remotes and cables out of sight, but check how far the lid opens. Next to the CANMOV, the ANJ puts more emphasis on the home theatre look and on ports at hand.
products.bestFor: Movie nights and family rooms where wipe-clean upholstery helps.
pros: Two USB ports sit with the armrest controls
Two buttons keep the recline simple
Hidden armrest storage tidies remotes

cons: No heat or massage on this chair

products.name: Amada Power Recliner Chair, Synchronised Recline
products.description:
The Amada links its footrest and backrest in a synchronised mechanism with infinite recline positions. The footrest rises independently to some extent, and the chair has side pockets, cup holders and USB charging. The metal frame is described as tested through tens of thousands of recline cycles.

Infinite positions mean you can stop anywhere rather than at preset angles, a smoother feel than step-based chairs. The listing lacks seat dimensions, so confirm them before ordering. It leaves out heat and massage, which suits people who prefer a pure seating experience.

Steel framing is a practical choice for durability, though it adds weight to lift during setup. Against the Ketaiyou's swivel base, the Amada is simpler and has fewer parts to wear. Its pockets and cup holders match the basic kit found on the CANMOV.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a sturdy, simple chair with smooth infinite recline.

cons: Seat dimensions are not stated in the listing

buyingCriteria.explanation: Where the port sits determines whether the cable is usable. The ANJ puts two USB ports on the controls on the outer side of the armrest, which keeps them within a hand's reach. Check whether the ports are Type-A only, since many newer phones use Type-C. Look at the cable length needed from the port to the device as well.

A comfortable seat is the first requirement before any extra. The CANMOV lists a 23 by 23 inch seat and a 19-inch seat height, which are the clearest numbers here. Taller or heavier users should look at the MAHOMICO's oversized build. Verify the weight capacity on the maker's sheet.

Some chairs use a two-button recline, such as the ANJ, while others use synchronised infinite positions, as on the Amada. The Ketaiyou spans 90 to 160 degrees. More positions feel smoother but need clearance behind the chair. Choose the control layout the user will actually find easy.

Only the jonpony and the MAHOMICO offer lift assist in this lineup. A lift chair tilts the whole seat forward, which can make standing easier for some people. It is a heavier, more complex piece of furniture. Ask a therapist whether it suits the user, as needs vary.

PU leather on the ANJ wipes clean, while the jonpony uses breathable fabric. Material choice affects heat, cleaning and how long the surface looks good. Pets and kids favour wipe-clean covers. Fabric suits people who sit for hours in warm rooms.

The CANMOV, ANJ and Amada all include cup holders and storage. Check depth and position, and whether the lid or pocket interferes with the controls. Pockets keep remotes within reach. A cup holder that is deep enough prevents tipping on long evenings. Keep drinks well clear of the USB ports, because liquid near electrical parts is a risk that no listing spec removes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how many ports each chair lists and where they sit. The ANJ puts two ports on its armrest controls, while the Ketaiyou and Amada simply list built-in USB. Chairs that described only a generic port earned fewer points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat and size data
howWeEvaluated.description: The CANMOV leads on stated measurements with a 23 by 23 inch seat and a 19-inch height. Other chairs in the group leave out dimensions, which we noted. A missing dimension counted as a reason to verify, not as a flaw in the chair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motion and mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: Swivel, rocking, lift and synchronised recline were compared. The Ketaiyou offers 270 degrees of swivel and 90 to 160 degrees of recline, while the Amada leads on infinite positions. We weighed complexity against comfort.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upholstery and care
howWeEvaluated.description: Breathable fabric, leather-look and PU covers were compared on cleaning and comfort. The ANJ's PU leather is the easiest to wipe, while the jonpony's fabric breathes best. Buyer feedback on peeling or wear was considered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Overall positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: Each chair is placed by what it does best: CANMOV for plain seating, jonpony and MAHOMICO for lift, Ketaiyou for movement, ANJ for wipe-clean ports, Amada for simplicity. These are editorial judgments, not medical advice or measured results.

howToChoose.subheading: Lift Recliner vs Standard Power Recliner
howToChoose.intro: These two designs solve different problems.

cards.label: Lift recliner
cards.text: A lift base tilts the whole seat forward to help with standing. The jonpony and MAHOMICO use this approach, and both add massage and heat. Pick one when standing from low seats is a daily effort, and have a therapist check the fit.

cards.label: Standard power recliner
cards.text: These chairs only recline. The CANMOV, ANJ, Ketaiyou and Amada fall here, and they are lighter and simpler. Pick one if the user stands easily and mostly wants a comfortable seat with charging.

howToChoose.note: Whichever you choose, weight capacity and installation matter. Follow the assembly guide closely, make sure every bolt and plug is seated, and stop using the chair, and tell the seller, if it makes unusual noises or moves unevenly until the maker has advised you.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for port type, number of ports and how close they sit to the armrest. Type-C support is helpful for newer devices. A power cord that reaches the outlet and a tidy cable run reduce trip hazards.

howToChoose.note: Verify capacity and warranty terms on the listing before you buy. Makers often list one model in more than one seat size, as with the two CANMOV chairs at 23 by 23 and 24 by 20 inches, so read the dimension line carefully and compare the seat depth with the length of the user's thigh so the cushion edge does not press behind the knee. Keep order paperwork, since warranty claims usually need the model number.

faq.q: Can I add USB to a recliner that does not have it?
faq.a: Some recliners use a standard handset that can be replaced, and replacement controls with USB ports exist for certain plug types. Compatibility depends on the plug and the brand, so check the connector before ordering. If you are not comfortable with electrical work, ask a professional.

faq.q: Which power recliner is best for a small space?
faq.a: Look at overall depth and the clearance needed behind the chair when reclined. The CANMOV at 36 by 35 by 41 inches is a useful reference point. Swivel chairs such as the Ketaiyou need space around the base.

faq.q: Do USB ports charge as fast as a wall charger?
faq.a: Not always. Chair ports are built for convenience, so speeds vary and may be slower than a wall adapter. Check the listing for output details. A plug-in adapter is a good backup for a tablet.

faq.q: Are cup holders and USB ports safe near a drink?
faq.a: Keep liquids away from the ports and controls where possible. Spills on an electrical component are a risk, so wipe up quickly and unplug the chair if liquid gets in. Follow the maker's instructions for cleaning.

faq.q: How long do power recliners last?
faq.a: Lifespan varies with use, weight and care. The Amada's metal frame is described as tested through tens of thousands of recline cycles, which is a claim to read with caution. Keep the cord unstressed and avoid overloading the chair.

faq.q: Do I need a lift recliner or a standard one?
faq.a: A lift chair tilts the whole seat to help with standing, while a standard power recliner only reclines. The jonpony and MAHOMICO add lift. If standing is difficult, an occupational or physical therapist can help judge which style fits.

faq.q: What should I check before the chair arrives?
faq.a: Measure the doorway, the hallway turns and the final spot, because a chair that arrives boxed can be bulky. Confirm that an outlet is within reach of the cord without an extension lead stretched across the floor. Check the wall clearance the recline needs and the maker's stated weight capacity. Finally, keep the packing paperwork, since warranty claims usually need the model number and the order details.
